# Vortex - Implementation Status

> **Treat every count below as a dated claim, not a fact.** They are derived from the trees and go
> stale the moment a file is added or removed, silently — a markdown table cannot fail loudly. The
> counts are tracked and re-measured separately, out of this file; what belongs here is the
> *reasoning*: why a count moved, which findings turned out to be noise, what was measured and how.

> **Last updated**: 2026-09-07 (snapshot re-measured and the four tools re-run; previous full
> re-measure of every *module* table 2026-08-13 — those rows below still carry their 2026-08-13
> figures and several are known stale, see "Current Priorities")
> **Method**: filesystem snapshot plus targeted AS3/TS directory counts. Module rows count the
> **primary** tree (`WIN63-…-782849652/src/com/sulake/`) recursively against the matching TS
> directory. Message rows are the one exception: the primary tree keeps almost every
> incoming/outgoing/parser class under `src/unknowns/`, so those are counted against
> `win63_version/habbo/communication/messages/`, which has them laid out per category. The two
> methodologies were mixed silently in earlier revisions of this file — that is why some AS3 counts
> moved in the 2026-07-28 pass without any AS3 tree changing (`habbo/ui` 375 → 369,
> `habbo/roomevents` 347 → 448, `habbo/quest` 41 → 64).
> **Important**: the file counts in this document are **not** a member-level AS3 parity
> certification. A TS count greater than an AS3 count only means files exist; completion still
> requires reading the AS3 source and auditing public API, lifecycle, parser/composer behavior, and
> dispose paths. Since 2026-08-20 there *is* a mechanical member-level measure — see "Member
> coverage" below — but it answers "is anything missing", never "is anything right".
>
> The 2026-07-17 cross-module parity audit put a number on that caveat: 188 divergences across every
> system except `communication/`, in code that already existed and typechecked clean. File counts
> say nothing about whether the code runs. See "Cross-module parity audit" below.

things is worth less than five covering five, and any reading of this file that treats the total as
a score will get that backwards.

### The infostand's "Phase 1" note outlived its blockers (2026-09-20)

`InfoStandWidgetHandler.handleGetUserInfoMessage()` carried a header saying the peer half was
deferred on dependencies the port lacked. Every one had landed since: `IRoomSession.tradeMode` /
`roomModerationSettings` / `isPrivateRoom`, `ISessionDataManager.respectLeft` /
`respectReplenishesLeft` / `systemShutDown` / `isIgnored` / `getGroupBadgeId`, and
`IHabboGroupsManager.updateVisibleExtendedProfile()`. The note read as settled, so nobody looked,
and three things stayed dead in the UI for as long as it sat there:

- **`isIgnored` was never set**, so `AvatarMenuView` showed `ignore` and never `unignore` — the
  peer menu could start an ignore and could not undo one.
- **`canTrade`/`canTradeReason` were never set**, so the trade row was hidden on every peer
  regardless of the room's trade mode, and its tooltip never said why.
- **The trailing `GetRelationshipStatusInfoMessageComposer` was never sent.** `InfoStandWidgetHandler`
  already listened for the answer and `InfoStandUserView.setRelationshipStatuses()` already knew how
  to paint it; the whole heart/smile/bobba block was waiting on a request nobody made. This is the
  "ported but never wired" shape again — both ends written, neither joined.

Also restored with them: `respectLeft`/`respectReplenishesLeft`, `targetRoomControllerLevel` off the
room object's `figure_flat_control`, the three moderation predicates
(`determineCanBeMuted`/`Kicked`/`Banned` + the shared `determineModerationLevel` /
`checkUserWithRightsModerationLevel`), and `groupId`/`groupBadgeId`/`groupName`.

**The achievement score on the card was the server's, and the client was right to print 0.** The
infostand read 0 for a player whose extended profile showed 140. Both numbers come from the same
`PlayerSummarySnapshot.AchievementScore`, but the room avatar's copy is
`RoomPlayerAvatar.ActivityPoints`, which was declared `init`-only with a `= 0` default and *nothing
ever initialised it* — `RoomAvatarProvider.CreateAvatarFromPlayerSnapshot()` sets only
ObjectId/PlayerId and then calls `UpdateWithPlayer()`, which did not touch it. So
`RoomAvatarSerializer` wrote a hard 0 for every avatar in every room. Fixed in the emulator
(`ActivityPoints` is now `private set`, assigned in `UpdateWithPlayer()`, which is both the entry
and the player-update path). Worth reading twice before blaming a parser: the client's
`UsersMessageParser` was reading the field correctly the whole time. `RoomPlayerAvatar.IsModerator`
and `SwimFigure` are the same never-initialised `init` shape and are still 0/empty — `IsModerator`
has no source on the summary snapshot, so closing it needs a field there first.

**Chat bubbles, same day, unrelated cause.** Six chat styles rendered as an unstretched blob with the
text drawn outside it: `notification_red`, `notification_green`, `notification_wrong`,
`notification_correct_circle`, `notification_question_mark`, `notification_skull` (plus six `nft_*`).
Their regpoints never shipped, so `ChatStyle` came up with a zeroed 9-slice grid — left cap 0, right
cap = the whole bitmap, nothing stretchable — and zeroed text margins. The cause was one regex in
`tools/import-chatstyles.mjs`: `RAW_EMBED_RE` listed `png|gif|jpg|swf|mp3|ttf|xml` and every
regpoints embed is declared `_regPoints_txt$<hash>`, so all 46 of them failed the "is this already a
raw hash-bearing name" test, fell through to the `_SafeCls_N`-only obfuscated map, resolved to null
and were skipped. Adding `txt` takes the importer from 43/89 to **89/89 complete styles, 0
unresolved**. Worth remembering when the next asset family comes up empty: the importer *reports*
its own misses, and `node tools/import-chatstyles.mjs` (dry-run by default) prints them.

**The best signal of the whole campaign is not in the body diff at all: it is a comment.** The
broadcast stub was literally `// Show broadcast alert dialog` followed by a closing brace, and
that shape is greppable — a comment naming an action with no code after it. **Six in the port,
six of them real**, where the literals signal runs at one in three:

| | |
|---|---|
| `onBroadcastMessageEvent()` | a hotel-wide announcement displayed nothing — and the line above it was `message.replace(…)` with the result discarded, so a multi-line one would have arrived as a single run |
| `showCallCreatedNotification()` | did not exist: sending a call for help produced **no answer at all**, no receipt and no FAQ link |
| `onRoomMessagesNotification()` | "N messages were posted in <room>" parsed and dropped |
| `onDoorbell()` / `onFlatAccessDenied()` | ringing a closed door showed neither "waiting" nor "nobody answered" |
| `onCanCreateRoomEvent()` | the answer to the click: neither the form nor the refusal with its reason |
| `onRoomInfoUpdated()` | the message says a room changed without saying what; AS3 re-requests it, the port kept the stale data |

**Its sibling is the stale stub marker**, which the port has been bitten by before
(`project_todo_blockers_are_stale`): `RoomDesktop.roomEngineEventHandler()` was "will route to
appropriate handling when widgets are ported" — all 47 are — and it was the last thing between
the engine announcing game mode and any widget hearing it;
`HabboNavigator.openCatalogClubPage()` was "no-op until catalog is wired", while the method
immediately below it carried the same sentence and already called the catalog.

**The highest-yield search is now direct, not per-module.** Two of those were a parameter accepted
and ignored, so `--unused-params` looks for exactly that: a TS parameter named `_x` whose AS3
counterpart reads `paramN` at the same rank. The decompiler numbers parameters positionally, which
makes the correspondence mechanical. 49 across the port. The heuristic needed one correction —
the `_` prefix does not prove disuse, `CategoryListCtrl.refreshEntry()` passes a `_currentCount` it
named badly — so the TS body decides too.

**Six corrections to the probe itself, each with a fixture and a mutation check** (20 now, and
every rule is mutation-covered):

- `readInteger` → `readInt`. `IMessageDataWrapper` is identical on both sides but for that one
  name, and it alone reported 220 parsers: the parser layer went **467 findings → 50**, and the
  five that still name a missing read are inlined helpers, checked.
- Colours: the decompiler prints decimal (`13891476`), the port writes hex (`0xD3F794`), and AS3
  writes CSS (`"#336a95"`) where the port writes an int. A number now counts in any of its forms.
- A same-named class in two packages was resolved by guessing. `MeMenuSoundSettingsItem.as` exists
  under `habbo/toolbar/memenu/` **and** `habbo/ui/widget/memenu/`; an abbreviated citation matches
  both, and `updateSoundIcons()` was being compared against a different class. The TS file's own
  package decides now, the tree order breaks ties.
- An inline **return** type was read as the body: `getFurniData(o): {id: number; …} | null`
  measured its own type. The port is Allman-braced, so the body is the first brace that opens a
  line, at zero depth.
- Calls weigh half of literals in the ranking: three of four verified false positives were a body
  factored into a helper or a table. The hoisting rule must NOT be extended to calls — a method
  name is in its own file merely by being declared there, which would have hidden the
  `refreshBuilderStatus()` that was a real defect.
- Four notation gaps found by checking its own output, each worth a family of false positives:
  the constants index read only single quotes, so `WindowMouseEvent`'s **backtick**-declared
  members were unindexed and every switch using `WME_DOUBLE_CLICK` was reported; the decompiler
  **escapes apostrophes** inside double-quoted strings and the port does not; it expands
  `Math.PI` and `Number.MAX_VALUE` into their literals, and splitting `1.7976931348623157e+308`
  even produced a phantom "308".

**24 fixtures now, and every rule is mutation-covered** — including the two the mutation pass
caught as decorative, which is the whole reason to run it.

**Three whole-repo sweeps were tried on top of the per-module passes, and only one is worth
repeating.** The third was `--dropped-guards`: AS3 writes a guard as an early `return`, and the
two best finds of the campaign — the room commands with no rights check, the wired trade with no
requirements check — were exactly that. It does not survive contact either. Checked three deep,
three false positives: TypeScript compresses guards that AS3 spells out, `||` for three `if`s,
`?.` for a null check, an if/else for a closure that returned twice. The mode is kept because it
costs nothing on a single module, but it is not a backlog. `--unused-params` earned its place: it found the room-owner commands, the wall-item
pickup and the navigator's room rank, and its remaining 34 are mostly documented decisions that
only lacked the marker. The **size ratio is not a sweep**: a list of the 49 worst AS3-to-TS
statement drops was checked four deep and every one was a false positive — `getWidgetMessages()`
is 67 `push` calls against one `return [...]`, `contentLoaded()` and `applySpecialChatContent()`
are bodies factored into a helper, and the fourth was a trace used as a cross-reference rather
than a citation. Statement counts stay what the header calls them, a last-resort smell, and the
literals are the signal.

**A trace that cross-references rather than cites is the probe's remaining blind spot.** Twice now
a member carried `// AS3: X.as::otherMember()` to explain where a value comes from, and the diff
faithfully compared it against that other member's body. Both cost a full investigation to
dismiss. There is no rule that separates the two; the only defence is reading the citation before
believing the finding.

**And one hygiene hole the probe walked into.** `DoorbellWidgetHandler.processEvent()` carried its
trace inside a JSDoc block, so the probe compared the helper declared below it instead — and
`check-as3-trace.mjs` requires `// AS3:`, a line comment, so that member is untraced as far as
rule 30 is concerned. **530 traces in the port are written in JSDoc, 169 of them with no line
comment after**: that many members the traceability tool and the body diff both count as
unmeasured. One fixed here; the rest is a measured backlog item.

### A fifth measure: looking INSIDE a member (2026-09-19)

The four measures answer "is it there". None of them looks inside a body, and the dominant defect
in this port is no longer a missing method — it is a present, correctly named, correctly traced
method that dropped one line. `toggleCatalog()` without its two dispatches, `disabledStyles`
fading to 0.4 where AS3 fades to 0.5, `onBuildersClubFurniCount()` without `refreshBuilderStatus()`:
every one of those was found by a human reading the neighbouring member, which is chance.

`scripts/member-body-diff.mjs` measures it. What makes it possible HERE and not in an ordinary
rewrite is rule 30 plus the port's habit of keeping AS3's identifiers: a trace names the AS3
member, so the two bodies can be lined up and compared on the three things a port cannot rename
away — **string literals, numeric literals, and calls to names the port knows**. A value in the
AS3 body with no occurrence in the TS body is the lead.

Four noise sources had to be answered before the output was worth reading, and each is a real
property of this port rather than a hack:

- **An event name is referenced through its enum**, never as a literal (`.claude/rules` and the
  `feedback_events_use_enum_not_string` lesson). So every constant in the corpus that HOLDS the
  string counts as the string. Without this, every switch handler reports its whole switch.
- **One AS3 member, several TS declarations.** The port legitimately splits a 200-statement
  `processWidgetMessage` switch into a method per case; comparing each piece against the whole
  switch reported the other cases as missing from every one. Grouped and diffed as a union:
  6,406 → 6,102.
- **A value hoisted to a class constant** is not a value lost. A literal the member lacks but its
  file has is dropped (`UsersMessageParser.SWIM_COLOURS`, 32 colours, was the model): 6,102 → 5,610.
  `--strict` keeps them.
- **A `DEVIATION:` marker already answers the question** better than any count, so those members
  are excluded — 71 of them today.

**It found three real defects in the first module it was pointed at**, all in the crash-report
path, all invisible to the other four measures:

- `storeErrorDetails()` wrote `is_fatal`, `crash_time` and `error_ctx` and stopped. AS3 also writes
  `error_desc`, `error_cat` and `error_data` — the message, the category and the chained stack
  trace — plus the message-queue debug data and a memory line. **A crash report from this client
  said something had failed and nothing about what.** The three keys were already declared in
  `HabboErrorVariableEnum` and written by nobody.
- `update()` incremented `_invalidTimeCounter` and `_timeLeapCounter` and logged them. AS3 puts
  both into the report through `addDebugData`, which is the only place it ever reads them.
- `onRoomEnter()` never set `last_room`/`in_room`, so a report filed from inside a room said
  neither which room nor that the user was in one.

Four more members in the same module turned out to be genuine, undocumented deviations — the
`FlashExternalInterface.*` calls, which are calls *into the page that embedded the SWF* and have
no counterpart when the port IS the page. They now say so, which is both the honest marker and
what takes them out of the measure.

**Read it as a worklist, sorted, per module — never as a total.** Repo-wide it compares 31,222
members and reports 5,610, and the sampled precision is roughly one real finding in three to five:
in `habbo/tracking` it reported 14 and 3 were defects, 4 were undocumented deviations, the rest
were shape. A constructor whose work the port moved into `initialize()`, a helper folded into its
caller and a branch AS3 itself cannot reach all surface here. `.claude/rules/00-mandate.md` applies
to this output exactly as to any other audit: read the AS3 body before acting on a line of it.

#### What it is worth — measured, not asserted

A measure whose own error rate is unknown cannot be used to call a module clean, so the same day it
was built the probe was measured three ways.

**`--self-test`, 12 fixtures.** Every noise rule above was tuned by hand against the repository,
which means the next tuning can undo one and the output would simply get quieter — indistinguishable
from progress. The fixtures pin the four noise rules and the signals they must not eat (a dropped
dispatch, a dropped call, a changed threshold), plus the three body extractors.

**Mutation-checked, and one fixture was decorative.** Breaking each rule in a copy must fail
exactly one case. Two of three did; the split-switch fixture passed even with the union broken,
because its `file` contained both bodies and the *hoisting* rule was quietly covering for it. It
now carries only the first body. **A self-test that has never been shown to fail is not evidence** —
the same rule as the screenshot harness.

**Recall: 5 of 5 on the defects fixed by hand that day.** `--ts-root` points the TS side at a
`git worktree` of an older commit while the AS3 side stays put — `sources/` is gitignored, so the
trees are identical on every commit and the parent of a fix is a replay of the defect. Against
`247120bf^` the probe names all five: the ten missing `SEARCHTYPE_*` mappings (its top finding in
the module), `storeErrorDetails`, `update()`, `onRoomEnter()`, and `toggleCatalog()` — the last with
both missing dispatch literals and `trackGoogle` spelled out. It also flags `HabboCatalog.dispose()`
at 37 AS3 statements against 2, which nobody has looked at.

**And one miss, which is the most useful result of the three.** Replayed against `dfcb3ef4^` — the
2026-09-02 fix where a whole `reward_track_item` style was never built — the probe reports nothing.
Not a heuristic failure: `fillStyleTable()` traces to **PRODUCTION**, whose 2016 body has no
`reward_track` either, so the comparison was against a ten-year-old build and correctly found
nothing. **The probe's recall is bounded by where the trace points**, which is the same drift
`project_production_traced_parsers_drift` and the 2026-08-09 repointing of 3,684 traces are about.
It cannot repair the citation, so it counts them instead: **2,985 of 31,222 comparisons (9.6%) are
made against a non-primary tree**, and "no gap" on one of those is a weaker answer than "no gap" on
the other 28,237. That number is now in the header of every run.

### The marker backlog, emptied — and the tracking flags nobody was writing (2026-09-19)

`todo-inventory.mjs` read 9 `TODO(AS3)` and `as3-member-coverage.mjs` 5 absent public members, both
having risen from 0 with the Variable FX work. Both are back down: **1 marker, 0 absents.** Almost
none of it was porting; it was checking claims that had gone stale, which is the recurring lesson
of this file.

**Five of the nine markers were in `HabboTracking`, and four of the five were wrong.** Each said the
same thing — "the bus has no emitter in this port, so subscribing would be a listener with no
speaker". Measured:

- **The ten `SEARCHTYPE_*` navigator events.** `MainViewCtrl.sendTrackingEvent()` emits all eleven
  and has since it was ported; the marker predates it and was never re-checked. They are subscribed
  now, onto `legacyTrackGoogle("navigator", …)`. Two labels are not their constant lower-cased —
  `my_favorites` (no `u`) and `highest_score` — and are copied verbatim. AS3 subscribes ten of the
  eleven and has no case for `MY_FREQUENT_HISTORY`; neither has this.
- **The catalog bus.** Two of its four subscriptions were live all along (`CATALOG_PAGE_OPENED`
  from `CatalogNavigator`, `CATALOG_FURNI_PURCHASE` from `HabboCatalog`). The other two were the
  real gap and it was on the *emitter* side: `HabboCatalog.toggleCatalog()` never dispatched
  `HABBO_CATALOG_TRACKING_EVENT_OPEN`/`_CLOSE`, and skipped `trackGoogle("catalogue","open")` too.
  Both restored at AS3's own place in the method, outside the recycler branch this port guards on
  `_recycler`.
- **The help bus** is the one the marker got right, and for the wrong reason: nothing emits it
  *here*, and nothing emits it in AS3 either — `HABBO_HELP_TRACKING_EVENT_CLOSED`/`_DEFAULT` appear
  in the enum and in `HabboTracking`'s dependency list and in no dispatch site, in any tree. That
  is a faithfully dead pair, so it is ported, not skipped.

**And the whole mechanism was inert anyway.** The handlers switched on `eventType(args)`, which
reads the emitted payload — but all 28 emit sites call `events.emit(TYPE)` with no payload, so the
switch matched nothing and **not one error-context flag had ever been written**, after the pass
that existed to start writing them. The subscription already knows its own type; it now passes it,
`eventType()` is gone, and `_errorContextFlags` is filled at field-init rather than in
`initComponent()` (AS3 fills it before `super()`, and `setErrorContextFlag()` bounds-checks against
`length`, so a flag arriving early was dropped in silence).

`scripts/check-tracking-buses.mjs` failed on the help subscription, correctly by its old rule. The
rule was too strong: the defect is the port LOSING an emitter, so it now falls back to the primary
tree and separates "silent here" from "silent in AS3 too". 39 subscriptions, 0 real silent buses.

**The four remaining markers were not work.** `_lastRenderedDigitCount` (assigned once, read
nowhere in the AIR dump) and `resolveBitmapDataClassLayer()` (a base plus two overrides, no caller
anywhere) are dead in the source and ported as such — each now says so with the occurrence count
instead of promising a revisit. `WindowController.getGraphicContext()` keeps its marker: the two
overrides need draw-into-parent, which is the `WindowComposite` rewrite.

**`VariablesWebApiAddon` is ported** — the last AIR file outside VariableFx, and the one marker
that *was* work. 171 lines of add-on plus the `ApiKeySection` preset (120 l. AS3), `ButtonPreset.set
buttonText` and `IUserDefinedRoomEventsCtrl.getCurrentWiredId()`, both AIR-only members, and three
messages. Headers follow the raid-protection precedent and needed no reassignment this time: AIR's
composer 2819 and event 59 are unused in both tables of the WIN63 registry, in `HabboMessages.ts`
and in the emulator, so both keep AIR's own number, declared on both sides. **The server has
neither handler**: no key is minted, so the dialog builds and the generate button answers nothing.

**A live wire mismatch fell out of checking those ids.** The emulator sent
`VariableFxConfigUpdateMessageComposer` on **267**, which WIN63 spends on `FriendFurniCancelLock`
and the client registers as exactly that — so every Variable FX config push was decoded by the
wrong parser and no configured bar could appear. The client's own comment had recorded the correct
assignment (AIR 267 → 3390) and the emulator had not followed it. Fixed in `vortex-emulator`;
`VariableFxConfigRemove` has no composer there at all and is still owed.

The five absent members were three files: `dispose()`/`get disposed` on the guest-room-result
parser (AS3 answers `disposed` off the moderation settings being null — no `_disposed` flag, here
either), `HabboAir.createLoadingScreen()`, which is a `DEVIATION` and now says why (the screen is a
self-appending DOM overlay built in `index.ts` *before* `VortexApp`, so a constructor failure still
has somewhere to report), and the eight `WINDOW_STATE_*` constants, which existed only as magic
strings in `BitmapSkinParser.STATE_FLAGS` and are now the named surface that table is keyed off.

### A Vortex skin could not add anything without forking the dump (2026-09-17)

VortexCoin had no icon, so it needed a currency icon style — two `<template>`s, two `<layout>`s and
two `<window>` entries. The cost of adding them was forking **108 KB** of dump XML:
`App.readVortexSkins()` *replaced* a skin wholesale and replaced the element description wholesale,
so `src/vortex-skins/` could only hold complete copies of `habbo_skin_icon_set_xml` (42 KB) and
`habbo_element_description_xml` (66 KB). That directory had stayed empty since it was created,
which is the tell: a mechanism nobody could afford to use.

It merges now. `mergeSkin()` folds templates/layouts/states by name, `mergeElementDescription()`
folds entries by `(typeId, style)` — the pair `ElementDescriptorRegistry` looks a descriptor up by
— and `mergeByKey()` **substitutes in place** rather than appending, because both the skin renderer
and the registry keep the first entry they meet for a key: a replacement appended at the end would
lose to the dump's and be dead with nothing logged. The two authored files are now 55 and 25 lines.

Three things this turned up, all of the silent-failure kind this port specialises in:

- **A skin template can only draw out of an atlas.** `BitmapSkinParser.parseTemplateList()` resolves
  its bitmap with `atlases.get(assetName)` over a map built solely from `App.ATLAS_NAMES`, and
  returns `null` on a miss — a standalone PNG in the image bundle is not something this system can
  draw, and saying otherwise costs an invisible icon and no warning. Hence `vortex_icons.png`, a
  Vortex-owned sheet, and a new `ATLAS_NAMES` entry. A stale `vortex-client-assets.zip` degrades
  safely: `getImageBitmap()` returns null rather than throwing, so only the new icon goes missing.
- **Redefining `<variable key="asset">` in an authored skin repoints the whole dump skin.** The
  variables merge too, and the dump's 86 templates all resolve `asset="$asset"` through it. The
  atlas name belongs on the template.
- The name is normalised — `vortex_icons_png` and `vortex_icons` both reach the `vortex_icons`
  entry (`normalizeAssetName()`, `WindowXmlAssetParser.ts:414`).

`ActivityPointTypeEnum.getIconStyleFor()` needed no branch: an unknown activity-point type already
falls through to `currencyiconstyle.big.<type>` / `.small.<type>`, so binding the icon is two
external-variable lines. The art and the atlas are drawn by
`packages/vortex-client/tools/build-vortexcoin-icon.mjs`, which exists because `*.png` is gitignored
repo-wide — without it a fresh clone with no `--pack` behind it has no way to produce the icon at
all.

### Variable FX: the bar family draws (2026-09-13)

The second feature out of the AIR dump, and the large one — ~14,500 lines of AS3 for wired-variable
effects: bars, hearts, levels and numbers that hang off avatars and furniture and track a room
variable. 43 files and ~7,250 lines are in so far: the whole message layer (4 parsers, 4 events, 5
DTOs, headers 3388/3390/3391/3889), the engine plumbing through `RoomObjectFactory` /
`RoomEngine` / `RoomMessageHandler` / `MovingObjectLogic`, the renderer framework, and **the bar
family complete at 12 of 12 AS3 files**.

**The translation contract is Flash-to-Canvas and it is the whole risk.** `BitmapData` →
`OffscreenCanvas`; `ColorTransform` → `globalAlpha` when it is alpha-only and a three-pass
multiply + `destination-in` when it tints; `copyChannel(RED → ALPHA)` → an explicit pixel pass,
because Canvas has no channel copy. None of that is checkable by reading it, so every renderer is
rendered in headless Edge before it is committed and the image is looked at. Twice that caught the
*harness* rather than the renderer (a missing metallic asset the renderer correctly refused to
draw; `convertToBlob()` on a plain `<canvas>`), and twice the verification caught a wrong claim in
the doc comment rather than in the code — the `AnimatedScalar` speed cap bounds *cruising* speed,
not per-step displacement, and `needsUpdate`'s quantisation is an early `return true` that can only
ADD a redraw reason, never filter one.

Where a claim is checkable by pixels, it is asserted rather than eyeballed: the striped bar's scroll
wraps exactly at 700 ms (phase 0 and phase 700 are pixel-identical) and really moves at 350 ms; the
arrow bar's `segments` override gives 141 px at 15 and 906 px at 999 — the cap at 100 — and falls
back to the size default on junk; the thermometer renders RED and CYAN pixel-identically, which is
the proof that it genuinely ignores the config colour.

**Nine bars, and no two of them draw the same way.** Classic and mini nine-slice a tinted fill;
health and boss vary the slices; block tiles; the striped bar scrolls a baked stripe layer and is
the family's only self-animating renderer (`isContinuous` is true only while there IS fill); the
arrow bar stamps one 11px chunk every 9px, the 2px of overhang being the arrowhead; the thermometer
tiles a single source PIXEL and never resolves a colour at all; and the heart memoises whole frames
by (colour, filled width) and is the one place the red-channel mask is used — the mask art is opaque
everywhere, so reading its alpha would mask nothing and the 1px leading-edge line would run past the
heart's outline.

**Two AS3 quirks ported deliberately, both noted at the declaration.** `parseExtraBoolean()` is a
stub returning null, so the `metallic` extra is read and discarded — that is the shipped behaviour.
`resolveDynamicLevellingRgb()` calls `.toLowerCase()` on a possibly-null `readExtra()`, a #1009 in
AS3; guarded here, because the faithful alternative takes the whole room's render down.

**All four renderer families are in, and the registry is closed.** 12 bar files, 3 health-point,
5 number, 9 level — 29 renderer files against 29 in the AS3 — plus
`VariableFxRendererRegistry.createDefault()`, which was deliberately held back until every factory
existed. It registers the 14 classes by name, then the 17-entry `(category, style)` fallback table,
then binds the server's numeric ids on top; that order is load-bearing, because both later steps
look factories up by name.

**The first end-to-end exercise of the feature** ran against the SHIPPED
`variablefx_renderer_mapping.xml`: all 15 cases construct, update and draw, and all 15 resolve by
server id rather than falling through to the style table. Before that every renderer had only ever
been driven directly by a harness.

Four things worth knowing about the families beyond the bars:

- The **heart stack** is the first renderer whose FRAME RESIZES, and its
  `AnimatedHeartOpacities` moves an array rather than a value — each heart gets its own fade window,
  staggered, so the stack fills left to right and empties right to left. The total is sub-linear by
  construction: one heart is exactly `SINGLE_HEART_ANIMATION_MS` and any number asymptotes to
  `MAX_ANIMATION_DURATION_MS`, so losing twenty at once is a sweep, not a twenty-times-longer one.
- The **number displays** are the same renderer with opposite trades — one tints a grey sheet per
  colour, one picks a source Y in a sheet the artist already coloured. The second buys exact control
  over five palettes and silently falls back to `GREEN` for anything else.
- The **level family** animates a level and its progress as ONE scalar, the "path" = level +
  progress, so a level-up is continuous motion rather than a bar jumping to 0 while a badge flips.
  A maxed level folds into the same number.
- `LevelWithProgressRenderer` is the only renderer that BUILDS ANOTHER RENDERER, through the
  registry, from a `sub_renderer` id. All four ways that can fail leave the bar null and render the
  badge alone — deliberately: a mapping the client does not understand should cost the bar, not the
  badge.

**The visualization wiring is in** — `StackedAdditions` + `VariableFxStackAddition` +
`VariableFxStackReconciler` into `AvatarVisualization`, with the per-room config table threaded
through `RoomObjectVisualizationFactory` and `RoomManager`. That is what puts a bar on screen.

**And so is the Wired editor**, the ~3,400 lines that let anyone configure one: 6 model files, 9
presets, the add-on base and its six subclasses. The last of those is what the user actually sees
first, because until the six codes existed `prepareForUpdate()` logged *"no ported element for code
1202 in addon"* and the dialog never opened.

The add-on base is one form over one state object; the six differ by a code and a category id, and
two of them by a single extra int param. **The param layout is the contract and it is not what the
field order suggests**: three values are written as LONGS, two slots each, so writing pushes 0..9
plainly, `defaultMinValue` into 10-11, `defaultMaxValue` into 12-13, four flags into 14..17,
`audienceVariableValue` into 18-19 and `segments` at 20 — and reading therefore skips 10, 12 and 18.
Levelling adds a sub-renderer id at 21, the number display an icon alignment.

**That count is what found two server-side breaks, both of which made a save fail silently.** The
emulator declared 21 rules for all six, and `TryNormalizeIntParams` rejects a count it has no rule
for and returns `false` from the whole update — so levelling progress and the number display, the
two that send 22, could never be saved at all. `GetMaxVariableIds()` was also still the default 0,
which let exactly one of the three variable ids through (`GetValidVariableIds` adds before it
tests). Both fixed in `vortex-emulator`. The three ids are positional on the client's side and the
shared pruning still drops the empty slots between them, which is noted where the limit is raised
— a display using only its audience variable reads it back as its minimum override.

The dialog's **header source-type selector is not wired**: `HeaderPreset` in this port takes no
`SourceTypeSelectorParam`, so the furni-or-user switch AIR puts in the header has nowhere to go yet
and the add-on's own `getHeaderSourceTypeSelectorParam()` has no caller.

### Raid protection, and a second asset source (2026-09-13)

A new dump landed, `sources/AIR-1.0.31/` — a later client than the primary, script-only at first
glance. `compare-as3-revisions` against the primary says what it is: **nothing removed**, 84 new
readable classes, 76 of them one feature (VariableFx), and the rest raid protection plus the wired
`VariablesWebApiAddon`. It is *not* a header source: only **16 of 586 composers keep their number**
across the two builds, 421 composers and 523 events move, and 78 / 85 change shape at the same
number. The emulator is pinned to the primary's numbering, so an id lifted from AIR is wrong on
this wire even when the message is right. CLAUDE.md now says so at the table row.

Raid protection is the first feature ported out of it: 2 composers, 3 events, 3 parsers, a wire
DTO, `RaidProtectionSettingsData`/`Controller`/`View`, and six wiring points (`HabboNavigator`
dependency + construction + getter + link case + dispose, `HabboNewNavigator`'s link case,
`LegacyNavigator`'s delegating getter, `IHabboTransitionalNavigator`, and `RoomInfoViewCtrl`'s
button + `RPSE_STATE_CHANGED` subscription + click). All **69 members** of the three AS3 classes are
ported — 24 / 13 / 32, checked one by one, no `TODO(AS3)`.

Headers had to be *assigned*, which is new here and worth the precedent: composers keep AIR's own
206 and 2687 because both are free in this revision and in the emulator; the events could not,
since two of three collide (AIR's 734 is `ChatReviewSessionOfferedToGuide`, its 3620 is
`SecondsUntil`). They are 3553 (AIR's own), 3554 and 3555 — the first ids after it unused as an
event *and* as a composer in the WIN63 registry, in `HabboMessages.ts`, and in the emulator. The
rule and the table are written into `HabboMessages.ts` itself.

**Three things this cost, each a measurement that contradicted a confident guess:**

- The AIR dump's assets are in `scripts/binaryData/`, and that was missed — a full window layout
  was *authored from scratch* before anyone looked. The real one is 430×488 with cards, an
  `itemlist` that resizes, a warning banner and a green Save; the invention was none of those.
  Look in the dump before drawing anything.
- The gap between the two trees measured by filename read 302, then 225. The real number is **1**.
  AIR's blobs carry the embed's *linkage* name (`border_12_xml$…`), the shipped assets carry the
  `*Com.as` *field* name (`habbo_skin_border_12_xml`) — exactly the collapse CLAUDE.md warns about,
  done in the other direction. Only the builder's own join can answer this.
- `HabboConfigurationManager` emitted `'configurationLoaded'` while its enum said
  `'HCE_CONFIGURATION_LOADED'`. Nothing listened to either, so the drift was invisible until the
  first subscriber — which would have been born dead.

`build-window-assets.mjs` now reads AIR as a **supplement**: it adds names the primary lacks and
never replaces one, except `AIR_PREFERRED`, which holds `iro_room_details_framed_xml` alone and for
one reason — the AIR copy differs by exactly one line, the `raid_protection_settings_button`.
Shipped layouts 788 → **789**. `--no-air` builds without any of it.

**Not done, and the feature cannot run without it:** the emulator has no raid protection at all —
5 headers, a handler that reads/persists/echoes, and the detection itself. And **none of this has
been exercised**: it typechecks and lints, the window has never been opened.

The texts are no longer owed. They were never missing upstream — habbo.com's live texts file has
all 47 `raid.protection.*` and 4 `notification.raid.*`, and the reason this hotel's copy lacked
them is that `sources/external_flash_texts.txt` is an older dump. `locale-overrides/
upstream-missing.en.txt` carries the whole delta the client can actually reach — 312 keys, of
which 209 are `wiredfurni.params.*` (the Variable FX editor's own labels) and 51 raid — and
`--merge-into` puts them on the host. The 40,253-key gap it does *not* close is the four
provenance rules the builder drops on purpose: 20,220 badge strings, 8,634 quests, 8,564 landing
campaigns and 2,498 promo offers, every one of them keyed by something this server hands out and
seeds none of.

### Doors and windows were cut by guesswork, and the thickness settings did nothing (2026-09-05)

Four faults in the room's plane renderer, found one behind the other. They are listed in the order
they were fixed, which is also the order they hid each other.

**`PlaneMaskManager.updateMask()` was a stub that returned `true` without drawing.** Every door and
window in the port therefore fell back to `getMaskHolePoints()` — a screen-space rectangle one tile
wide by `DOOR_HEIGHT_TILES = 2.5` tall that never reads `mask.type`, so every opening in the game
was the same rectangle whatever the artwork said. The manager also never received an asset
collection: `RoomVisualizationData.initializeAssetCollection()` forwarded textures to the two
rasterizers and stopped there, so even a working `updateMask()` would have resolved nothing.
`RoomEngine.onRoomContentReady()` now builds a `GraphicAssetCollection` off the same spritesheet and
hands it over — masks need an *asset*, not a texture, because a mask has to be positioned and a bare
canvas carries neither offset nor flip flags.

The measurement that settles whether this half works is a log line, not a screenshot:
`RoomVisualizationData` reports the resolved mask types at room load. A live room answers
`29 mask type(s): door, bolly_wdw_wd, hween08_wndw, …`. Zero would mean the artwork never arrives
and everything downstream is moot; the line exists so nobody has to guess again.

**The room's wall and floor thickness settings reached nothing.** `RoomPlaneParser` has
`floorThicknessMultiplier` / `wallThicknessMultiplier` and no caller anywhere in the port had ever
set them, so the room-settings sliders changed a model variable that died there.
`RoomVisualization.updatePlaneThicknesses()` now reads both and resets the planes, and
`initializeRoomPlanes()` hands them to the parser before parsing.

Two regressions came out of that fix and are worth keeping written down, because both were the port
misreading its own order of operations rather than the AS3:

- The call was first placed inside `updatePlaneTexturesAndVisibilities()`, which runs **after**
  `initializeRoomPlanes()`. `resetRoomPlanes()` then destroyed the planes one line past the rebuild
  and the room went black about two seconds in. AS3 runs the thickness check at `update()` l.601-609,
  *before* the rebuild; the ordering is the whole point of where it sits.
- `resetRoomPlanes()` disposed planes whose textures published sprites still held, and pixi threw
  `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'alphaMode')` on the next frame. Sprite textures are now
  detached before the dispose.

**A resolved mask type is not resolved artwork.** With the asset path live, `applyBitmapMasks()`
recorded a mask as asset-masked whenever `getMask(type)` answered — and `updateMask()` returns
`true` even when the type has no visualization for that plane's scale and facing, because AS3's
does. The polygon fallback was skipped for masks that had drawn nothing, so a doorway that used to
be a crude rectangle became no opening at all. It now asks `getGraphicAsset(scale, normal)` and only
claims the mask when there is something to draw.

**What actually made the doorway vanish: `reset()` was missing one field.** Everything above is
real, and none of it was the reported bug. AS3's `resetRoomPlanes()` ends by calling `reset()`, and
AS3's `reset()` nulls six fields where the port nulled five — the missing one being `_maskXml`, the
cached mask XML that `updateMasksAndColors()` compares against before re-applying masks. Rebuilding
the planes throws their masks away with them; leaving the cache standing means the fresh planes
never get doors or windows, and no later update can repair it because the XML never changes again.

The omission was inert for as long as nothing rebuilt planes mid-session. `updatePlaneThicknesses()`
does, so the symptom arrived with the thickness fix and read as "the door rendered for two frames
and then the wall went solid for good" — which is exactly what it was. Two lessons, both already in
this file in other words: a field-by-field diff against the AS3 body is worth more than reading it
for sense, and a latent gap surfaces when an unrelated change starts exercising it.

Three measurements settled this, after two wrong diagnoses that were reasoned rather than measured:
the mask-type log line (29 types, artwork reaches the planes), a probe printing the placement
numbers (`place=112,115`, asset offset `-16,-86` → the cut lands at texture (96,29)-(128,115), which
is correct), and a decode of `HabboRoomContent.nitro`'s own pixels (`door_64` is 32x88 and every one
of its 2,816 pixels is opaque black, so the mask is a rectangle and the port's alpha-based cut and
AS3's `darken`-on-RGB cut agree). With all three green the remaining candidate was the one nobody
had looked at.

**The doorway reveal is a deliberate deviation, and it is `near \ far`.** Neither AS3 nor Flash
Habbo draws the inside faces of a cut opening: their mask punches a flat hole through a wall that
has thickness everywhere else, so an open doorway shows the void behind the room. The port fills it,
projecting the mask's own alpha twice — once pushed back along the plane normal by the wall
thickness — and subtracting the far copy from the near one. That subtraction order is the geometry
of looking through a hole: what you see through is where the two openings overlap, and the rest of
the near opening is tunnel wall. Written the other way round the band lands *outside* the hole, on
the solid wall, which is how it shipped first.

> **Removed 2026-09-20, by the project owner's call.** 174 lines: `drawMaskReveals()`,
> `projectThickness()`, `REVEAL_COLOR`, `_revealCanvas`, `_revealOffset`, `_maskShapeCanvas`,
> `RoomPlane.wallThickness` and its one assignment in `RoomVisualization`. The port is closer to
> AS3 for it — this had no counterpart in either tree. **Confirmed on screen: removing it also
> removed the grey band reported at the doorway's foot.** The reveal was the cause.
>
> Recorded because the reasoning that argued otherwise was wrong and was written down first: two
> pixel measurements off a screenshot — "the band is 64 px wide where a reveal would be ~16" and
> "it draws in front of the entrance tile while the opening draws behind, so they are on different
> planes" — were both used to conclude the reveal was innocent, and both conclusions were false.
> The 16 px figure was invented: the band's screen width is a *projected* 3D offset through the
> plane's affine transform, not `0.25` tile measured in tile units. Measuring the right pixels
> does not make the inference from them sound.
>
> Still true and still useful: `RoomVisualizationData` logs the mask count at room load, production
> hides `info`, so only the zero-mask `warn` is visible — and its absence is how we know masks
> resolve at all.

### The WIN63 file-level sweep (2026-09-02) — what is actually left, and the six gaps it found

Counting uncited `.as` files against the primary tree is the wrong measure taken alone, and the raw
number says so: 8,049 filenames, 4,842 with no citation anywhere in the port. Almost none of that is
code. 1,767 are the flat `_SafeCls_N.as` embed wrappers at `src/` root, 1,069 are `binaryData/`
asset libraries, 15 are Flex/`deng` framework, and 1,047 are `unknowns/` DTOs largely ported under
recovered names. What is left is **947 uncited files under `com/sulake/`**, and splitting those by
whether a TS file of the same name exists at all gives the only two numbers worth quoting:

| | files | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| ported, no `AS3:` citation | 448 | rule 30 never applied there; their member coverage is unmeasurable |
| absent, obfuscated name | 340 | mostly messages ported under recovered names — `wire-coverage` reads 0/0 |
| absent, readable name | 138 | the only honest shortlist |

Of those 138, most are deliberate: 36 `*Bootstrap.as` are empty SWF entry-point subclasses
(`RoomEngineBootstrap extends _SafeCls_90` and nothing else) that `VortexMain` replaces with direct
DI, ~25 are AIR/profiler/Flash-platform, 12 are the notification feed (dead in AS3 — flag off *and*
controller never constructed), and 5 are `ui/widget/messages/` classes nothing constructs. The real
remainder was two blocks — the catalog and Discord Rich Presence — plus a handful of room files.

Closed in this pass:

- **The seven unbuilt catalog widgets.** `CatalogPage.createWidget()` fell through on
  `builderAddonsWidget`, `builderLoyaltyWidget`, `builderSubscriptionWidget`, `roomPreviewWidget`,
  `traxPreviewWidget`, `trophyWidget` and `userBadgeSelectorWidget` — every name was already in
  `CatalogWidgetName`, nothing constructed the class. The switch is now 48/48 against AS3's.
- **`CatalogWidgetBuilderSubscriptionUpdatedEvent` and its dispatcher**, which no ported class
  raised. Both AS3 call sites are restored, and `onBuildersClubFurniCount()` was additionally
  missing `refreshBuilderStatus()`.
- **The two NFT furni logics.** `FURNITURE_NFT_CREDIT` and `FURNITURE_NFT_REWARD_BOX` were
  registered in `RoomObjectFactory` — to the base `FurnitureLogic`. The enum was wired, the
  behaviour was not.
- **`FurniturePlanetSystemVisualization`**, an empty class body the factory had been handing out
  since it was written.
- **`HabboLandingView`'s `HTIE_ICON_GAMES` case**, the landing-view half of the pair whose navigator
  half was ported.

~~Still open and deliberately so: **Discord Rich Presence**~~ — **closed 2026-09-06** (`3fa9ffb3`).
`habbo/discord/` holds the manager, its IID, `habbo_activity/` (detection + state) and `settings/`
(controller + view); AS3's ANE talking to the local Discord IPC pipe becomes the local RPC
WebSocket, the only transport a browser can reach. Two gates, and they are different: the transport
sits behind `discord.rpc.enabled` (default off — Discord closes the socket `4001 Invalid Origin`
unless the application has an RPC-origins grant it no longer hands out; measured 2026-09-06, see the
`DEVIATION:` on `initialize()`), while the settings dialog sits behind `discord.enabled` and works
regardless.

Two notes for whoever re-runs this. The measure has one systematic false positive worth knowing
about: an obfuscated file ported under a recovered name reads as "absent" by basename unless its TS
cites it, so the 340 need `wire-coverage`/`sweep-unwired` to be judged, never the filename alone.
And the 448-file untraced bucket is the larger finding — it is what makes 9,271 members unmeasurable
in `as3-member-coverage.mjs`, and no amount of porting shrinks it.

### The hidden member worklist (2026-09-02) — 74 absents, and why most were not

`as3-member-coverage.mjs --unmeasured` counted 74 public/protected members absent from files the
port cites only at file level, and would not name them. It now does. The list was mostly an
attribution artifact: a TS file citing *one* member of an AS3 interface was being charged with that
interface's whole surface — `FurniIconImageManager` cites `getProperty()` off the config interface
`_SafeCls_53.as` and was answerable for its other six. Ownership now requires a basename match, or
sole citation when the AS3 name is obfuscated.

What survived the triage was four real defects, all in `core/window/dynamicstyle`: the
`reward_track_item` style was never built (`fillStyleTable()` registers five, the port registered
four), `brightness_and_shadow_under` and `..._gentle` pressed their icon with `offsetY: -1` where
AS3 has `1` so it rose instead of sinking, `disabledStyles` faded to 0.4 against AS3's 0.5, and
`AvatarUpdateEvent` carried a constant `AVATAR_UPDATE` that exists in no tree — AS3 passes
`super("AVATAR_FIGURE_UPDATED")`, which is what the landing-view widget listens for, so the editor's
save never reached it. That last one had been written up in a comment as an AS3 quirk; it was not.

The rest is dead AS3 (`stageChangeResize` is registered nowhere, `mouseCursorType` is an empty
override returning 0, `defineCustomCursorType` has no caller) or narrowing already argued at the
declaration. Each now says so where a reader looking for it will land.

**A rename is not a deviation.** Four members had been renamed and the rename then documented with
a `DEVIATION:` marker, which is backwards — the marker is for behaviour the port changes on purpose,
not for a name it changed for no reason. `populateWithStrings` is `populateWithVector` again across
its 16 call sites, `getChildStyleByTags(tags)` takes the `WindowController` AS3 takes,
`setChildStyle()` gives way to the public `childDynamicStyles` map every style registry writes
through, and `pressedStyles` goes back to the source's own `pressedSyles` typo.

### Boot ordering (2026-08-16) — the asset library was empty for every component in `prepareCore()`

Fifteen `Asset not found` / `no bitmap asset` / `not in the asset library` warnings at boot, and all
of them one cause: `App.ts` registered the images from `initClientUi()` — *after* `connect()` — and
the layouts right after `Vortex.bootstrap()` returned. Every component built inside `prepareCore()`
therefore read an empty library. AS3 cannot have this bug: `HabboWindowManagerComponent(context,
flags, assets)` is handed an `AssetLibrary` already filled from its `[Embed]`ed SWF resource.

The channel already existed and already documented this exact reasoning —
`IVortexConfig.windowAssets`, which is how skins/atlases/layouts were handed in. It now also carries
`imageUrls`, `libraryImages` and `libraryLayouts`, and `VortexMain` seeds the library in
`registerWindowAssetLibraryContent()`, called immediately after `new AssetLibrary(ctx)` and before
any `attachComponent`.

Three things the fix turned up that are worth keeping:

- **`registerAssetUrl()` was a silent no-op before `initComponent()`.** `HabboWindowManager`
  creates its `ResourceManager` in `initContexts()`, so the image URLs — which must go in *before*
  the manager is attached — landed on a null field and vanished. They now buffer into
  `_pendingAssetUrls`/`_pendingAssets` and replay when the ResourceManager is built.
- **`HabboUserDefinedRoomEvents` was constructed without an asset library.** AS3's third
  constructor argument is forwarded verbatim to `WiredMenuController`, `WiredChestController`,
  `WiredTransactionLogsController`, `WiredTransactionDetailsController` and
  `RewardNotificationController`. Dropped, `Component.assets` stayed null and
  `WiredChestWrapperView` could not find `chest_generic_xml` — the chest window was never built at
  all. Same omission previously fixed for HabboGroupsManager, HabboCatalog,
  HabboSoundManagerFlash10 and HabboFriendBar; this was the last one.
- **Fire-and-forget decoding is a race, not an optimisation.** The library bitmaps were registered
  from an unawaited `.then()`; `getAssetByName(...).content` is read synchronously, so
  `add_friends_icon` missed whenever the friend-list packet beat `createImageBitmap`. They are
  awaited now.

Two warnings in the same log were **not** bugs and must not be "fixed":

- `illumina_light_border_top_center` is declared by no `*Com.as` in any tree — the layouts reference
  it, the client never shipped it, and AS3's `IlluminaBorderWidget.getPiece()` skips a null piece.
- `No container found for widget: RWE_ME_MENU` — the port matches
  `DesktopLayoutManager.getWidgetContainer()` line for line, and the `memenu` layout carries no
  `room_widget*` tag, so AS3 returns false here too (silently; only the port logs it).

#### `RoomEngine` dropped a room asked for before the engine was ready — fixed

`Cannot create room — manager not initialized (state: 1)` was the one boot warning left, and it was
a whole unported mechanism. AS3's `initializeRoom()` opens with `if(!_SafeStr_5461)` and **parks**
the room in `_SafeStr_5320` — `RoomData`, name recovered from PRODUCTION, keyed by room identifier
and carrying floor/wall/landscape type and camera position — then `roomManagerInitialized()` replays
the lot once the manager reports ready. The port called `createRoomInstance()` immediately, got null
and dropped the room forever. It is what killed the `RoomPreviewer` inside the chest window, built
at DI time long before `RoomManager` finishes loading its placeholder object content.

Three pieces, all from the primary tree:

- `RoomData` (`habbo/room/utils/`), the parked entry. Obfuscated to `_SafeCls_1852` in the primary
  tree, which is where the *member* names are readable; PRODUCTION obfuscates those and predates
  `cameraInitPosition`, but gives the class name. The four door values are TS-only: AS3 re-reads
  the door out of the parked room XML, this port takes it as separate `initializeRoom()` arguments,
  so the queue has to hold them to replay the same call.
- `updateObjectRoom()`'s buffering branch, which parks a floor/wall/landscape push arriving before
  the room object exists. It carried a `TODO(AS3)` saying it could not be ported because
  `win63_version` decompiles it into `null.floorType = param2` — the primary tree has it intact.
  This is the third time that rule has paid (see "win63_version is a worse decompile").
- `RoomPreviewerWidget`'s `REE_INITIALIZED` subscription (AS3 l.68-71, `onRoomInitialized` l.201),
  which the port had not ported at all. Without it the deferred room is built and no canvas is ever
  attached to it.

Also folded in: `initializeRoom()` now feeds the parked floor/wall/landscape types to the three
`RoomObjectRoomUpdateMessage`s instead of the hardcoded `"111"/"201"/"1"`, which is what AS3's
`createRoom(param3, param4, param5)` does with them; and the `data == null` early return, which
becomes load-bearing once a `updateObjectRoom()`-only entry can be replayed with no plane parser.

Verified headlessly: before the room manager reports ready the preview room sits in `_roomDatas`
(`parked: ["room_2147418115"]`, `built: []`, no warning); after, `parked: []`, `built:
[2147418115]`, and `getRoomInstance(2147418115)` returns a real instance.

### The room-users packet was parsed against a 2016 build (2026-08-16)

`Parse error for 996: End of buffer` in `UsersMessageParser`, at a `readString()` inside the
per-user loop. The parser was transcribed from `PRODUCTION-201601012205-226667486`, and the 2026
client reads **one more field** at the end of every type-1 (player) avatar:

```as3
_loc16_.achievementScore = param1.readInteger();
_loc16_.isModerator      = param1.readBoolean();
_loc16_.badgesRank       = param1.readInteger();   // absent from the 2016 build
```

Both sides agree that field exists: the primary tree reads it
(`src/unknowns/_SafePkg_2184/_SafeCls_2309.as::parse()` — obfuscated, found by its `_users` field
and `IMessageParser`), and the emulator writes it
(`RoomAvatarSerializer.SerializePlayerAvatar`, `.WriteInteger(snapshot.BadgesRank)`). Not reading it
left four bytes per player in the buffer; the next iteration consumed them as `webId` and every
field after that was one slot out, until a length-prefixed string read a garbage length and ran off
the end. With one avatar it merely left junk; it corrupts from the second onward, which is why it
surfaced during 100-avatar testing.

`RoomUserData._badgesRank` already existed, carrying a comment asserting that "the initial
room-users list simply doesn't carry it" — read off the same 2016 build. Taking that note at face
value is what kept the field unwired.

Verified by bundling the real parser with esbuild and feeding it packets encoded exactly as
`RoomAvatarSerializer` writes them:

- without the read — `RangeError: End of buffer`, 0 users, **139 bytes** left unconsumed
- with it — 3 players parsed, **0 bytes** left, every field on the right value
- a mixed player + pet + bot packet also lands exactly, so the type-2 and type-4 branches match the
  emulator too

Fixed in the same pass, same root cause: `convertSwimFigure()` was also the 2016 version. It
hardcodes the swimsuit colour to `10001` and always emits a swim type, where the 2026 client derives
both from the wire value (`…=<name>/<r,g,b>`) against a 32-entry colour table — and leaves both at
`1` when the string carries no `=`. The file's five AS3 traces were repointed from PRODUCTION to the
primary tree.

### `|| 1` ate every infinite animation loop (2026-08-16)

Reported as "the dragons' flame isn't animated". `rare_dragonlamp` is
`furniture_multistate` / `furniture_animated`; its flame is **layer 5 of animation 1** — four
frames, `frameRepeat: 2`, `loopCount: 0`. In this format `loopCount: 0` means *loop forever*:
`AnimationLayerData` stops a layer only on `loopCount > 0 && loopIndex >= loopCount`.

`AnimationData.initialize()` read it as `(layerDef['loopCount'] as number) || 1`. JavaScript treats
`0` as falsy, so every infinite loop became a single pass. AS3 does not have the bug because it
tests for the attribute's *presence*, not its truthiness:

```as3
_loc7_ = 1;
_loc10_ = _loc5_.@loopCount;
if(_loc10_.length > 0) { _loc7_ = int(_loc10_); }   // "0" is kept as 0
```

Measured on the real `rare_dragonlamp.nitro`, walking the frame counter the way
`updateFramesForAnimation()` does:

- before — `[1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4,4,4,4,4,…]`: one pass, then held on the last frame forever
- after — `[1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4,1,1,2,2,…]`: loops

This was never dragon-specific: it silenced the loop on **every** furni whose animation declares
`loopCount="0"`, which is the normal way to write a continuously animated layer.

The same absent-vs-zero mistake was swept for in the visualization parsers and found once more:
`PlaneMaskManager` read `parseFloat(bmpData.normalMinX) || -1`, where AS3 guards with
`if(String(@normalMinX) != "")`. A normal coordinate of exactly `0` is a legitimate bound, and
collapsing it to `±1` widened the mask's range so it matched planes it should not have.

### Two AS3 type tests the port turned into unchecked casts (2026-08-16)

Same transcription habit behind both: AS3 leans on `as` and on implicit nullability, TypeScript's
equivalents *assert* rather than test, and the null arrives anyway.

- **`ProductGridItem.setDraggable()`** — `interactive.setMouseCursorForState is not a function`,
  which took down every catalog page carrying a `ClubGiftWidget`. AS3 writes
  `if(_view as IInteractiveWindow && param1)`, and its `as` yields **null** when the object does not
  implement the interface: that line is a runtime type test. `as unknown as IInteractiveWindow` is a
  compile-time assertion that never yields null, so every view reached there was taken for
  interactive — and the club-gift item hands over its plain `image_container`. `IInteractiveWindow`
  is erased at runtime and implemented by four unrelated controllers, so the check is for the member
  the method actually uses.
- **`ITableObject.getTableCell()`** — `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'type')` at
  `TableCellView.initializeView()`, thrown inside the window manager's update receiver. AS3 declares
  `:TableCell`, but object types are implicitly nullable there and every implementation returns null
  from its default branch. Transcribed non-nullable, each of the eleven had to launder that through
  `null as unknown as TableCell`, and `TableCellView` was left dereferencing a null it had been told
  could not exist. The signature is now `TableCell | null`. This is exactly what the `TODO(AS3)` on
  `TransactionPreviewTableObject` called the real fix, and why it deferred it.

AS3 survives the unguarded deref because every `getTableCell()` covers every column its table
declares — the default branch is unreachable there, and **statically unreachable in this port too**:
all eleven were checked against their tables' `TableColumn` ids and every one matches. So the trigger
is not a column mismatch, and it was not reproducible. A null cell therefore renders empty and logs
which column and which row object produced it; if that warning ever appears, the fix belongs in that
row object's `getTableCell()`, not in `TableCellView`.

### The transverse-debt pass (2026-08-14) — a stale asset, a four-module sweep, three wrong headers

Three items off the "Not yet done" list, and one find that was not on any list.

#### The avatar configurations were the 2016 build, and two of them were not shipped at all

`packages/vortex-client/src/assets/configurations/` is gitignored — derived dump content,
regenerated per checkout — but **nothing regenerated the avatar XMLs**. They had been copied in by
hand from `PRODUCTION-201601012205-226667486` and never refreshed. Measured against the primary
dump:

| Asset                  | Shipped        | Dump   | What was missing                              |
|------------------------|----------------|--------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `HabboAvatarAnimation` | 21,405 (2016)  | 56,253 | the `Default`, **`Lay`** and **`Sleep`** actions |
| `HabboAvatarGeometry`  | 15,996 (2016)  | 19,020 | `petl`/`petr` + all 8 `order-before` attributes |
| `HabboAvatarPartSets`  | 5,746 (2016)   | 7,380  | the `misc` and `pet` activePartSets           |
| `HabboAvatarFigure`    | 5,345          | 5,345  | — already current                             |
| `action_offset_lay`    | **absent**     | 278    | `App.ts` asks for it; the lookup returned null |
| `action_offset_swim`   | **absent**     | 486    | likewise                                       |

All three stale files are **strict subsets** of the dump's — nothing was removed between the
builds, only added — so the swap could not regress anything. `AvatarActionManager.ts:187` already
reads `'action_offset_' + state`: the code was ported and waiting on an asset nobody shipped, the
same shape as every other entry under "Ported but never wired".

The fix is `packages/vortex-client/tools/import-avatar-configurations.mjs`
(`pnpm --filter vortex-client import:avatar-configurations`), so it stays fixed across checkouts.
**Why there was no importer: `loadCryptedManifest()` only scans `*Com.as`, and these six embeds are
declared by `HabboAvatarRenderLib.as`** — a `SimpleApplication`, not a component manifest, so
`findComFiles()` never sees it. Any other embed declared by a `*Lib.as` is invisible to
`import-crypted-images.mjs` and `import-crypted-sounds.mjs` for the same reason; that is worth a
sweep of its own.

The tool also brought in a seventh file the port had no idea existed:
`dance_sixseven_animation`. AS3 registers it from
`AvatarRenderManager.registerBuiltInAnimations()`, called out of `onAvatarActionsLoaded()` right
after `updateActions()` — **that method was not ported at all**. It is now, along with its
`BUILT_IN_ANIMATION_ASSET_NAMES` constant, and the asset name is in both
`EMBEDDED_AVATAR_XML_ASSET_NAMES` lists.

#### The ported-but-never-wired sweep, four modules

Recipe as documented under priority 0, with one correction: **matching a handler name anywhere in
the module produces false negatives**, because a same-named method on another class of the module
satisfies the grep. `onActivityPoints` read as present in `habbo/quest` purely because
`QuestController.onActivityPoints()` exists — the registration was missing. The reliable form
resolves each AS3 `_SafeCls_N` through the registry to its **id**, then asks whether that id's
event class is constructed in the port's handler.

| Module               | AS3 registrations | Missing before | Missing after | What they were |
|----------------------|-------------------|----------------|---------------|----------------|
| `habbo/friendlist`   | 12                | 0              | 0             | clean — the candidate named in priority 0 has no gap |
| `habbo/quest`        | 24                | **8**          | **0**         | all eight events existed *and* were registered; nothing subscribed |
| `habbo/notifications`| 36                | 11             | 9             | 2 wired; the other 9 need the message ported first |
| `habbo/groups`       | 22                | 3             | 2             | 1 was a correct deviation, 1 a documented Phase-1 cut, 1 an unported message |

`habbo/quest` is the clean case and the largest: `ObjectAdd`/`ObjectRemove`/`ObjectRemoveMultiple`
and `RoomSettingsSaved` all drive `roomCompetitionController.onContextChanged()`;
`AchievementsScore` publishes the score as the `achievements.categories.score` localization
parameter; `ScrSendUserInfo` starts the room competition on VIP + responseType 2;
`IsFirstLoginOfDay` and the whole-wallet `ActivityPoints` (which zeroes every
`ActivityPointTypeEnum` before applying the wallet) close it out. Every target member —
`onContextChanged()`, `sendRoomCompetitionInit()`, `setIsFirstLoginOfDay()`, `registerParameter()`
— was already ported. It was eight `addMessageEvent` lines.

Two of the three `habbo/groups` findings **did not survive verification**, which is the rule
working as intended:

- `onUserObject` caches the own-user id in AS3; the port's `get avatarId()` reads
  `_sessionDataManager.userId`, fed by the same message. A correct deviation — now commented at the
  getter so the next sweep stops re-flagging it.
- `onRelationshipStatusInfo` needs `ExtendedProfileWindowCtrl.refreshRelationships()`, which the
  file's own header records as a deliberate Phase-1 scope cut, not an accident. The message layer
  (event, parser, `RelationshipStatusInfo`, `RelationshipStatusEnum`) is fully ported and ready.
- `onBadgeLeaderboardResult` is genuine: id **2503** is in no client registry.

#### The last three modules, swept 2026-08-14 — and the recipe mechanised

`habbo/toolbar`, `habbo/navigator` and `habbo/session` were the three the section above named as
not yet swept. They are done, and the sweep is now a script rather than a procedure, because
running it by hand is what let two findings hide.

| Module           | AS3 subscriptions | Missing before | Missing after |
|------------------|-------------------|----------------|---------------|
| `habbo/toolbar`  | 3                 | **1**          | 0             |
| `habbo/navigator`| 55                | **1**          | 0             |
| `habbo/session`  | 75                | **6**          | 1 (documented)|

**Two corrections to the recipe, both of which changed the result:**

1. **"Constructed somewhere" is not the question — "constructed by *this* module" is.** A first pass
   asking only whether the TS event class is built anywhere in the engine reported toolbar and
   navigator clean and found 2 in session. Narrowing it to the module found 8. This is the
   `ActivityPoints` lesson again, one level up: `UserRights` is constructed by four other modules,
   `HabboGroupDetails` by three, and each was still missing where AS3 also subscribes it.
2. **Strip comments before matching.** A commented-out registration reads as a construction. Two
   findings sat behind the identical line `// TODO: Register additional message events when
   implemented` — `RespectNotificationMessageEvent` in `RoomChatHandler` and `DanceMessageEvent` in
   `RoomUsersHandler` — with the event, the parser and the registry entry all already in place.

What the seven were:

- **`RoomChatHandler` was 7 of AS3's 10.** `RespectNotification` (chat type 3) and
  `HandItemReceived` (type 5) were ported and unsubscribed; **`SpecialSystemChat` (id 3102, type
  12) had no message at all** and is newly ported — event, parser, registry entry. Its name is
  **derived, not recovered**: `win63_version` is older and does not carry it, and the emulator has
  no constant for 3102 either, so it is named for the AS3 handler (`onSpecialSystemChat`); this is
  stated at both declarations. `RoomSessionChatEvent` was also missing `CHAT_TYPE_PING` (11) and
  `CHAT_TYPE_SPECIAL_SYSTEM` (12).
- **`RoomUsersHandler`** now dispatches `RoomSessionFriendRequestEvent` — `FriendRequestWidgetHandler`
  had been listening for it since it was written — and `RoomSessionDanceEvent`.
- **The dance round trip is closed at both ends.** `AvatarInfoWidgetHandler` now handles `RSDE_DANCE`
  as AS3 does (own avatar only, matched on room object id), and the optimistic `isDancing` the port
  set at the *send* site is gone. Checked before removing it: the emulator's `DanceMessageHandler`
  is real and `SetAvatarDanceAsync` broadcasts `DanceMessageComposer` to the whole room, sender
  included — so the echo genuinely arrives.
- **`HabboNewNavigator._groupDetails` was never filled.** `onGroupDetails()` and
  `getCachedGroupDetails()` were both written; nothing called them. `onGroupDetails` is now on
  `IHabboNewNavigator`, reached through a new `HabboNavigator.newNavigator` getter — the same shape
  as the existing `transitionalNavigator` one, and for the same reason.
- **`HabboToolbar.addHabboConnectionMessageEvent()` was dead code** — helper, tracking list and
  disposal all ported, never called once. AS3's single toolbar subscription is `onUserRights`, whose
  whole body is a second attempt at `initVideoOfferExtension()` (the first runs from
  `onPerksUpdated()`, before `catalog.videoOffers.enabled` may have flipped).

**The one left open is deliberate and now carries a `TODO(AS3)` at `RoomSessionManager`:**
`onRoomVisualizationSettings` (2986) returns immediately unless `_roomViewerMode`, the standalone
room-viewer embed this port does not implement. The message is ported and `RoomMessageHandler`
subscribes it for the normal path.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean on both packages, ESLint clean on every touched file, and the sweep
re-run reports 0 missing in toolbar and navigator, 1 documented in session.

#### The ten "server is waiting" send gaps, triaged — 2026-08-14

`wire-coverage` reported 10 send gaps with a real (non-stub) emulator handler behind them, which
reads as a ready-made worklist. It is not one, and the difference matters before anyone plans around
that number: **a send gap is only cheap when the code that would send it is already ported.**
Resolving all ten through WIN63's registry to their AS3 composer, then to the class that sends it:

| id   | composer sender (AS3)                          | what it actually costs |
|------|-------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| 394  | `HabboInventory.initComponent()`                | **done** — wiring      |
| 2069 | `HabboInventory.initComponent()`                | **done** — wiring      |
| 3862 | `FurniModel.requestInitialization()`            | needs `_isInRoom`, i.e. `roomEntered()`/`roomLeft()` and the three handlers that call them |
| 2931 | `ClubDiscountPromoExtension.onTextRegionClicked()` | that click handler is not ported |
| 1760 | `AchievementsResolutionController`               | the port's is a 177-line log-only shell |
| 916  | `AchievementsResolutionController`               | same |
| 3426 | `BCFloorPlanEditor`                              | ported 2026-08-28; measured before that |
| 880  | `BCFloorPlanEditor`                              | ported 2026-08-28; measured before that |
| 625  | `VariableManagementDetailView`                   | the `habbo/roomevents` remainder |
| 785  | —                                                | **not a client gap** |

**Two of ten were wiring.** `GetSilverMessageComposer` (394) and `GetNftCreditsMessageComposer`
(2069) — both of which kept their real names through obfuscation — did not exist in this port at
all, so the two balances were never requested once. They are now sent from `initComponent()` where
AS3 sends them. Send gaps 47 → 45, real-handler gaps 10 → 8.

**785 is not a gap at all.** It is absent from *both* tables of `_SafeCls_2046.as`: the emulator
carries a header this client build does not have. Two others nearly went the same way for the
opposite reason — a first pass reported 394 and 2069 as absent from the registry because the grep
assumed obfuscated `_SafeCls_N` names, and those two are in clear. **Match both forms.**

`HabboInventory.initComponent()` also revealed a question this pass deliberately did not answer: AS3
sends five composers there and this port sends none, reaching 540 through `requestFurni()` and
`habbo_club` through `onPurseTimer()` instead. Adding the boot sends without checking those paths
would double every request rather than close a gap; the marker at that site says so, and
`_SafeCls_2019` has no port equivalent under any name.

#### `variables_management/detail` — the permanent-variable editor, 2026-08-14

The first of `habbo/roomevents`' enumerated remainders, and the slice that closes send gap **625**
from the triage above: editing the wired variables stored on one user, pet or bot.

What was there: `VariableManagementDetailController` as a 53-line spine against a 267-line original,
its interface, and nothing else. No view, no previewer, **and no message layer at all** — events
1557 and 1643 unregistered, composer 625 absent, `WiredUserPermanentVariablesList` non-existent.
Both ends of the chain were already live, which is why this was worth doing before anything else in
the module: `WiredMenuController` constructs the controller, and the overview's row click already
sent 3777 to ask for the data that had nowhere to go.

Ported: the DTO, two parsers, two events, the 625 composer, `PermanentVariableHolderPreviewer`
(130 l.), `VariableManagementDetailView` (490 l.) and the controller's remaining 214 lines.

**All four names are recovered, not derived.** `win63_version` carries readable filenames for every
one — `WiredUserPermanentVariablesEvent`, `WiredSetUserPermanentVariableResultEvent`,
`WiredSetUserPermanentVariableComposer`, `WiredUserPermanentVariablesList` — which is the
"read `win63_version` filenames first" rule paying off again. It also caught a false claim already
in the tree: `RequestVariableManagementDetailComposer` (3777) documents itself as "fully obfuscated
in AS3", where `win63_version` names it `WiredGetUserPermanentVariablesComposer`. Corrected at the
declaration; the class is left unrenamed to avoid churning its call sites.

Three details worth keeping:

- **The owner block on the wire is conditional.** `WiredUserPermanentVariablesList` reads owner
  id/name/figure only when `entityType != 1`, because a user is its own owner. Reading them
  unconditionally would consume the variable count as the owner id and desynchronise everything
  after it.
- **One message does all three writes.** Edit, create and delete are all 625, separated by a `mode`
  of 0/1/2. Delete still carries a value, and AS3 sends 0.
- **Two sources have to agree before anything draws.** The wire sends variable ids and values, never
  what those variables *are*, so `onGetData()` asks the synchroniser for the catalogue first and
  applies the list in the callback. A stored value whose definition is unknown is dropped rather
  than rendered.

`Util.windowIsChild()` was added while porting the view's click-outside handling: AS3 has it as a
member of every window (`WindowController.windowIsChild()`) and this port's `IWindow` does not, so
`WiredMenuInspectionTab` had grown a private copy. Both now share one, and the tab's copy is gone.
(`TableRowView` keeps its own — AS3 declares one on that class too.)

Send gaps 45 → 44, real-handler gaps 8 → 7.

#### The chests tab — 2026-08-14

Second of `habbo/roomevents`' enumerated remainders: lock/unlock the room's wired chests, and a
ten-row preview of their recent transactions.

It was a 31-line stub against 264 lines, `TransactionPreviewTableObject` was missing, and its
message layer did not exist — event 2910, composers 2016 and 1630, and the two DTOs. All of it is
ported, plus `TransactionConfig` (14 lines, one integer) out of the deferred
`wired_trading/transactions/overview` block, which is the only thing the tab needed from there.
**That dependency looked like a blocker and was not** — worth checking before deferring a slice on
the strength of an import list.

Two things the port had to get right:

- **One header answers two windows.** 2910 feeds both this tab's preview and the paged transactions
  window, and the payload says which: a page is only the preview's if `amount` is 10, `currentPage`
  is 1 **and** `logListType` is 1. The two `logListType` names are derived — 0 is read by
  `WiredTransactionLogsView`, 1 by this tab, and that is all the evidence there is.
- **Nothing pushes a chest transaction**, so the tab polls: `update()` re-requests every 20 seconds
  while it is being viewed. The lock buttons also go quiet for 500 ms after a click, so a double
  click cannot send the same command twice.

**The server knew nothing about chests** when this was written. Unlike camera and crafting — which
at least have handlers that accept and drop — vortex-emulator had **no constant at all** for 2910,
2016 or 1630, so they did not even register as send gaps in `wire-coverage`. The tab was complete
client-side and mute in practice. That is a third category worth naming: *not implemented* is
visible in the gap count, *stubbed* is visible once the script reads bodies, but *absent from the
header table* is invisible to both.

> Superseded 2026-08-23: chests are served now — contents, settings, logs, withdrawal, the furniture
> deposit and the contract offer. See "The chest a player could look into but never fill" below.
> What that closes is the *mute* half; the tab itself never changed.

Names: `WiredTransactionInfo` and every accessor on it are recovered — that class survived
obfuscation. Everything else here is **derived**, and says so: `win63_version` predates wired chests
entirely (not one chest message anywhere in it) and the emulator has no constants to corroborate
against.
